raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this season the way I always do...

---

I've been farming this land for 60 years. My father did it before me. Sixteen mu and a bit — not big, but it's enough when me and the old woman are careful. Our son works in town, sends money sometimes, but the farm is ours to manage. Three mouths to feed and whatever we can sell at the market.

I do wheat and maize like everyone in the village. Wheat goes in after the October holidays, comes off in June, then maize goes right in behind it. Same as always. Same as my neighbor Old Wang, same as everybody. No point changing what works.

**On the wheat:** I put down compound fertilizer before planting — about one bag per mu of the 15-15-15 stuff, sometimes a bit more if I have it. Then when the wheat is jointing in the spring and looks a little yellow, I spread urea, maybe 15 kg per mu. My nephew told me last year to use less, but I've always done it this way and the wheat looks good. Too little and you can see it — the leaves don't green up right. I'd rather spend the extra money on fertilizer than have a thin crop.

Water for wheat — I water after planting if it's dry, once in winter if the ground is hard, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. That's how my father taught me. Pumping from the well costs money but you can't skip the jointing water.

**On the maize:** After the wheat combine comes through in June, I have maybe a week to get maize in the ground. I hire the seeder because I'm too old to plant by hand on this much land. I use the hybrid seed from the agricultural store — everyone uses it now, the old seed is gone. Base fertilizer goes down with the seed, then one topdressing of urea when the maize is knee-high. Maize doesn't need as much water if the summer rain comes — usually I water once or twice if it's dry.

**What I can't do anymore:** Climb on the combine, carry heavy bags all day. I hire the combine for wheat harvest, hire the tractor for tilling. My wife helps with weeding and watching the irrigation. For maize picking we hire two-three days of help from the village.

**Costs worry me.** Fertilizer keeps going up. I don't buy pesticide unless I see bugs or weeds — herbicide I use because otherwise the bindweed chokes the wheat. Insecticide I only spray if I see aphids or armyworm. No fungicide, never bought it.

Yield? On a normal year wheat gives me maybe 450 kg/mu, maize about 500 kg/mu. Good year a bit more, bad year less. Last year was okay.
